ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Jesse Owens

code.originalText: Six weeks after left upper lobectomy: pathology, surveillance plan, tobacco remission and pulmonary rehabilitation

text.paragraph: Six weeks after left upper lobectomy: pathology and the plan from here. [S]

Mr. Owens returns six weeks after his thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy. He went home on the third day, needed no opioid after discharge, and stopped acetaminophen two weeks ago. Pathology shows only 0.7 cm of residual cancer with 6 percent viable tumor, a major pathologic response, with clear margins and no cancer in any of 16 lymph nodes. Dr. Halvorsen-Pierce reviewed the options with him last week. He walks 2 km a day and starts the pulmonary rehabilitation program next week. He gets mildly short of breath on two flights of stairs. He has not smoked for four months. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-09-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 74.6 kg; blood pressure 122/76, pulse 76; oxygen saturation 96 percent
Breath sounds slightly reduced at the left apex; no crackles; port-site incisions healed

Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting screening finding in a long-term smoker. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration
S — Synthetic histology, stage and biomarkers linked to his documented adenocarcinoma of the left lung; in the modern episode it is found by screening while still resectable.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking; superseded at the visit after surgery by nicotine dependence in early remission.

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (rhinovirus on a respiratory panel) on day 13 of cycle 2 of chemoimmunotherapy: runny nose, sore throat and a dry cough for three days, no hypoxia, clear chest X-ray; immune-related pneumonitis and pneumonia excluded; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.
After thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with mediastinal and hilar lymph node dissection: ypT1a N0 (0 of 16 nodes), R0, major pathologic response (6 percent residual viable tumor)
S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic operation.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, in early remission: no cigarettes since day 1 of cycle 1, about four months, on varenicline
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking.

list.item:
Left upper lobe adenocarcinoma after chemoimmunotherapy and lobectomy (C34.12). Curative-intent treatment complete, with a major pathologic response and no residual nodal disease. More immunotherapy after surgery is an option used in other trials, but the regimen he received was designed to be given before surgery only, and the major response predicts a low risk of recurrence; after hearing the options from Dr. Halvorsen-Pierce, he chose surveillance. The KRAS G12C result stays on file in case of recurrence. [S]
Surveillance: history, examination and chest CT every six months for two to three years, then yearly low-dose CT.
No routine brain MRI, PET-CT or blood tumor markers for surveillance.
Pulmonary rehabilitation program from next week.

After left upper lobectomy (Z90.2). Recovering well; mild exertional breathlessness expected at six weeks. [S]
Pulmonary rehabilitation for 12 weeks.

Nicotine dependence in early remission (F17.211). Four months without a cigarette after 35 years; this is a major part of his cancer care. [S]
Continue varenicline to complete 24 weeks.
Relapse-prevention calls from the quitline.

TSH on nivolumab. TSH 4.6 with a normal free T4: settling after the grade 1 thyroiditis, no treatment needed. [S]
TSH and free T4 again in three months.

list.item: PET-CT, brain MRI, EBUS staging, tissue diagnosis, PD-L1 and comprehensive biomarker results and a tumor board plan within three weeks of the screening CT. Outcome by 2026-05-26: PET-CT in three days, brain MRI in four, EBUS in eight, tumor board in ten; PD-L1 and tissue sequencing back by the consultation, 15 days after the scan [S]
Stop smoking completely before treatment starts and stay stopped. Outcome by 2026-09-30: No cigarettes since day 1 of cycle 1, about four months; varenicline continued to complete 24 weeks [S]

Three cycles of chemoimmunotherapy before surgery without a delay of more than one week and without an immune-related adverse event of grade 2 or higher. Outcome by 2026-08-05: Three cycles on schedule; only a grade 1 rise in TSH, monitored without treatment [S]

Complete resection (R0) with systematic lymph node dissection within six weeks of the last cycle. Outcome by 2026-09-30: Thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy five weeks after cycle 3; R0; major pathologic response [S]
Back to walking 3 km most mornings by three months after surgery. Outcome by 2026-09-30: Walking 2 km a day six weeks after surgery and starting pulmonary rehabilitation [S]
